chapter: Jack Laine and the New Orleans scene
title: Jack Laine's hold on the city and slapping the bass
summary: Laine had the city's musicians sewn up; he first slapped the bass with the Rhythm Kings about 1922.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, let's come back to the Orange Wheel ahead of us ourselves, don't we? Uh, supposedly said that you were around 17 or 18 years old. You were playing a lot of music then, huh?
Did you have a regular outfit then?

No, you see, Jack Lane, he practically had the city sewed up as far as musicians are concerned and workers are concerned. So there wasn't an overabundance of good men. Of course they used to call them squeegees. The guys that really couldn't hit the ball, they called squeegees. Uh, they did call, referred to fiddle player as a squeegee fiddler. Well, he had no bow technique or anything, and he'd get off on tones and things like that. Well, I wanted to ask you too, when you were a kid
playing bass, did you use a bow? Oh, yes. When did you start slapping it? Do you remember?
